ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Constant, worsening lower-midline abdominal ("tummy") pain for a few days, rated 8/10.
• Symptom details:
  – Onset/duration: Began a few days ago; progressively worse; pain present all the time.
  – Location: Midline, below the umbilicus (lower abdomen).
  – Severity: 8/10.
  – Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding after normal period ended 2 weeks ago; occasional nausea (no vomiting); constipation last week (now resolved); small amount of vaginal discharge; no fever, chills, dyspnea, shoulder pain, syncope, dysuria, hematuria, hematochezia, weight loss.
  – Aggravating/alleviating factors: None specified; pain simply "gets very bad."  
• Past medical history: No chronic illnesses; no previous surgeries; no prior pregnancies.
• Medications / allergies: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) placed 1 year ago; allergic to amoxicillin.
• Family/social history: 23-year-old female teacher; lives with husband and in-laws; sexually active; no smoking, alcohol, or recreational drugs; travel abroad >1 year ago.
• Vital signs / exam: Not performed (tele-visit).
• Labs / imaging: Home pregnancy test negative 1 month ago; no other studies yet. Plan to repeat pregnancy test and schedule in-person abdominal exam.

V: Ectopic pregnancy (tubal rupture risk → vascular bleed): lower abdominal pain + light vaginal bleeding + reproductive age
Ovarian torsion: acute/worsening constant pain, can be midline initially, vascular compromise of ovary
I: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): lower abdominal pain, vaginal discharge/bleeding, sexually active
Appendicitis: early mid-abdominal pain that can stay midline, nausea, worsening course
N: Hemorrhagic or ruptured ovarian cyst: sudden/worsening pelvic pain, light bleeding possible
Uterine fibroid with degeneration: pelvic pain and abnormal bleeding
D: Severe constipation/functional bowel disorder: recent week-long constipation causing abdominal pain
I2: Hormonal-implant side effects: irregular bleeding and mild pelvic discomfort possible
A: Endometriosis: chronic pelvic pain, dyschezia/constipation, abnormal bleeding
T: Occult abdominal or pelvic trauma (no history given, less likely)
E: Early intra-uterine pregnancy with threatened miscarriage (hormonal/metabolic changes): pelvic pain + light bleeding

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Reproductive-age woman with constant worsening lower abdominal pain and post-period light bleeding; last pregnancy test was a month ago and failure rate of implant, although low, exists. Must be ruled out urgently because of morbidity.
supporting_evidence: Lower abdominal (pelvic) pain of acute onset, getting worse
Light vaginal bleeding unrelated to expected menses
Sexually active, contraception failure possible, no recent pregnancy test
opposing_evidence: Pain described as midline rather than unilateral; no shoulder-tip pain or syncope yet

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: PID commonly causes bilateral lower abdominal pain, light bleeding, vaginal discharge and nausea in sexually active women.
supporting_evidence: Light vaginal bleeding and small amount of discharge
opposing_evidence: No dysuria, dyspareunia, or cervical motion tenderness reported (exam not done)
Implant use may reduce STI risk via barrier? (behaviour matters more)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Acute constant pelvic pain that worsens can stem from torsion or cyst complications; may present midline initially and light bleeding may occur with cyst rupture.
supporting_evidence: Severe constant pain (8/10) increasing over days
Light vaginal bleeding can accompany cyst rupture
opposing_evidence: No sudden onset described; more gradual over days
No vomiting or marked GI upset often seen with torsion

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Early appendicitis may present with midline lower abdominal pain and nausea, progressing over days.
opposing_evidence: Pain localised to midline lower abdomen, not RLQ migration

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Recent week-long constipation could have caused pain, but bowels now normal and pain persists/worsens making this less likely.
supporting_evidence: History of significant constipation last week
opposing_evidence: Presence of abnormal vaginal bleeding not explained
